# webjmail

> webjmail is a fast, local-first, open-source JMAP email client with a built-in
> calendar. It runs in the browser or as a native desktop app (Linux, macOS,
> Windows) and works with any JMAP server — Stalwart, Fastmail, or your own
> self-hosted mail. Passwords are held in a native, age-encrypted vault and never
> touch the browser.

webjmail is for people who want a modern webmail for a JMAP server without a
third-party service in the middle. It is not tied to a provider: you enter your
email address, it autodiscovers `/.well-known/jmap`, and connects directly to
your server.

Key facts:
- Protocol: JMAP (RFC 8620/8621) for mail, JMAP Calendars (JSCalendar, RFC 8984) for calendar.
- License: open source under AGPL-3.0-only, plus a commercial Enterprise License from Rotko Networks. Source at https://github.com/rotkonetworks/webjmail (may trail the hosted build).
- Platforms: web app, plus desktop builds via Tauri (Linux AppImage/deb/rpm + AUR, macOS, Windows); Docker image for self-hosting the web app.
- Privacy: local-first (on-device index, works offline); credentials stay in a Rust-side age-encrypted vault; the landing page and app make no third-party requests.
- Cost: free.

## Docs
- [Home](https://webjmail.com/): what it is, features, downloads.
- [Web app](https://app.webjmail.com/): the hosted client — enter your JMAP email to connect.
- [Self-hosting / CORS setup](https://webjmail.com/#connect): how to point webjmail at your own Stalwart server, including the Caddy/nginx CORS config the browser build needs.
- [Download](https://webjmail.com/#download): desktop builds (AUR, AppImage, .deb, .rpm, .dmg, .msi), Docker, and source.

## Source
- [GitHub repository](https://github.com/rotkonetworks/webjmail): full source, issues, releases.
- [Releases](https://github.com/rotkonetworks/webjmail/releases): desktop binaries.
- [Container image](https://github.com/rotkonetworks/webjmail/pkgs/container/webjmail): `docker run` the web app.

## Common questions
- Is webjmail a JMAP client? Yes — it speaks JMAP natively; there is no IMAP bridge.
- Does it work with Stalwart? Yes, it's built for self-hosted Stalwart (and Fastmail, and any JMAP server).
- Can I self-host it? Yes — run the Docker image, or build the static site and serve it yourself.
- Does it have a calendar? Yes — day/week/month views over JMAP Calendars, with timezones and drag-to-schedule.
